subject: BrightLeaf discovery follow-up — price calibration & host comps
messages:
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ari Patel <ari@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLeaf discovery follow-up — price calibration & host comps

Hi Ari —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we can align on economics and get this into procurement: 

Call highlights (short):
- Primary use: clinical-notes summarization + triage routing for ~50k weekly active users (expected ramp to 200k WAU over 12 months).
- Typical request: 300–800 tokens input, ~120–350 tokens generated.
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 700ms for patient-facing flows.

Volume & budget signals you shared:
- Current estimate: ~600M tokens / month in steady state (aggregate infer + system tokens).
- Near-term (Q4) target: 200–300M tokens / month.
- Budget range signaled: $6k–$18k / month initially (finance still validating).

Open ques for you (quick):
1) Can you confirm whether the 600M tokens/month estimate includes embeddings for search or is generation-only?
2) Do you have an internal target $/1M tokens (ballpark) that would make Redwood commercially attractive vs continuing with OpenAI/host providers?

For transparency, attached a quick snapshot we ran comparing unit costs at different host price points (redwood_pricing_snapshot.pdf). We included comparators at $18/1M, $12/1M, and $6/1M to show impact on monthly bill and required discounts for parity with Anthropic/OpenAI at typical host prices.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm embedding scope (Q1).
- We run a narrow performance/latency pilot on a small subset of flows (2–3 weeks) with measurement hooks — I’ll draft SOW.
- If pilot metrics look good, we prepare a 6–12 month reserved commit proposal with a target $/1M token tier to present to procurement.

Grace & Ben — internal ask: can you run a quick sensitivity showing break-even unit price vs host mix (OpenAI, Anthropic, self-hosted open models) for 600M tokens/mo and for 200M tokens/mo? I dropped a raw pricing matrix in attachments.

Ari — if you can reply with the two clarifications above and any procurement timing constraints, I’ll produce a short commercial one-pager.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: brightleaf notes referenced (BrightLeaf_MAAP_v2.xlsx), our pricing matrix (pricing_matrix.csv), redwood_pricing_snapshot.pdf
From: Ari Patel <ari@brightleaf.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 11:01:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: BrightLeaf discovery follow-up — price calibration & host comps

Jonas — thanks for the recap and the materials. Quick answers below and a couple of clarifications so you don’t over-index on worst-case numbers.

1) Volume composition: the 600M / month figure is a total system estimate and DOES include embeddings for search + internal analytics. Generation-only is closer to ~420M / month. We can provide a short export showing the breakdown by flow.

2) Internal target: Finance hasn’t given a hard target yet, but procurement leadership flagged they’d be happier if the unit worked to the equivalent cost of $9–$11 / 1M tokens for generation-heavy paths. For embedding-heavy workloads they’re modeling $3–$5 / 1M equivalent (embeddings are far cheaper per-op in our stack).

Procurement timing: they would like a pricing proposal in the next 2–3 weeks to align with a vendor shortlist review on Sep 1.

Notes: we are currently on OpenAI for most production (curie/ada equivalents for smaller flows, gpt-4 for complex summarization), and run Anthropic for a set of safety-critical transforms. We’re also piloting a small self-hosted LlamaX cluster for cost experiments but it’s not production-ready.

I’ve attached a lightly redacted product roadmap and the MAAP you requested. Happy to chat Wed afternoon if that helps.

—Ari
Ari Patel | Head of Platform
BrightLeaf Health
ari@brightleaf.ai | +1 (650) 444-1082
(Procurement looped in)
From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightLeaf discovery follow-up — internal pricing note

Jonas / Ben — forwarding Ari’s clarifications. Quick internal thoughts:

- Use-case breakdown changes things: 420M gen-only vs 600M total means our proposed reserved tiers should reflect a blended unit that separates generation vs embedding workloads. Offer hybrid model: $/1M_gen + $/1M_embed (embed lower).
- Procurement target band $9–$11 /1M for gen is achievable with a modest commit and 12–18 month reserved capacity. We should surface a two-tier proposal:
  * Conservative: 6 month pilot + month-to-month at $14/1M gen, $6/1M embed (no commit)
  * Reserved: 12 month commit at scale (>=400M gen/mo avg) at $9/1M gen, $4/1M embed + predictable SLAs and a 10% credits buffer for preview traffic spikes.
- Compare vs OpenAI: public list for similar models is running ~ $20–$25/1M (generation-equivalent) for higher-capability models; Anthropic similar. Self-hosted costs we show as $2–$7/1M but require ops overhead and likely not hitting reliability/latency targets.

Ben — can you produce a short table (2–3 lines) we can include in the one-pager that shows monthly cost at 200M and 600M for 3 scenarios (OpenAI list, Redwood reserved, Self-hosted ops-adjusted)? Put that in pricing_matrix.csv and link it for Jonas to share.

I’ll draft the two-tier commercial language and include the pilot SOW template.

Grace
Grace O’Connor | Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ari Patel <ari@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 15:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLeaf discovery follow-up — price calibration & host comps

Ari — thanks for the quick turnaround and the procurement timeline. Attached is a short one-pager and a simple cost table that maps to the bands we discussed (redwood_pricing_snapshot.pdf + pricing_matrix.csv). High-level commercial proposal for procurement review: 

Pilot (2–3 weeks)
- Scope: two patient-facing summarization flows (sampled traffic), synthetic load to validate P95 latency <= 700ms
- Price: trial run at $0.00 / token (no charge) for pilot instrumentation; Redwood covers pilot infra.

If pilot meets agreed SLOs -> Reserved proposal
- Term: 12 months
- Commit: 400M generation tokens / month (blended commit; embeddings carved out)
- Unit rates after commit: $9 / 1M generation tokens; $4 / 1M embeddings
- Overage: billed at $12 / 1M gen; $6 / 1M embed
- SLA: P95 latency target 700ms, monthly credits if missed (TBD in final SOW)

We’ve also included a competitive comparison row so procurement can see where this sits vs OpenAI/Anthropic public list pricing and a rough ops-adjusted self-hosted number. We’ll send a DocuSign-ready quote if Procurement confirms the commit band and timeline.

Next asks from Procurement: can you confirm whether the 600M number will be used for vendor shortlist comparisons (i.e., do you want us to model the commercial at 600M or at 420M gen-only)? Also — confirm contract owner and whether DocuSign routing should go to procure@brightleaf.ai or to legal@brightleaf.ai.

If agreeable, we’ll prepare the formal quote and a short SOW for the pilot by end of week.

Thanks — looking forward.
Jonas
--- End of thread ---
